modules.title: Enterprise AI Strategy and Architecture
modules.summary: Turn business strategy into constraints, decisions, dependency maps, and a resilient target state.

lessons.title: Architecture as a Portfolio of Decisions
lessons.summary: Manage AI capabilities, platforms, products, data, vendors, and controls as an evolving system.

contentBlocks.text: Architecture as a Portfolio of Decisions

Principal architecture connects business outcomes to reusable capabilities and explicit constraints. It avoids both one universal platform and uncontrolled duplication by defining shared primitives, domain-owned decisions, lifecycle stages, and triggers that revisit assumptions.
Principal-level reasoning
items: Map decisions by reversibility, blast radius, and option value.
Fund shared capabilities only when multiple products have durable common needs.

contentBlocks.text: A target architecture is a managed sequence of decisions and transitions, not a static future-state diagram.

challenge.prompt: Apply: Architecture as a Portfolio of Decisions
challenge.instructions: Choose the answer supported by reproducible evidence and principal-level trade-off reasoning.

choices.text: Define principles, capability map, decision rights, transition states, and measurable review triggers.

challenge.explanation: A target architecture is a managed sequence of decisions and transitions, not a static future-state diagram.
hints: Map decisions by reversibility, blast radius, and option value.

lessons.title: Build, Buy, Partner, or Defer
lessons.summary: Evaluate strategic differentiation, control, time, switching cost, risk, and total lifecycle economics.

contentBlocks.text: Build, Buy, Partner, or Defer

Vendor capability can accelerate delivery, while internal platforms provide control and leverage where requirements are distinctive. The decision should include integration, evaluation, security, migration, support, exit, and organizational capability—not just API unit price.
Principal-level reasoning
items: Identify which layer creates product differentiation and which is commodity.
Price the credible exit path and dual-running period before commitment.

contentBlocks.text: A reversible vendor choice with strong interfaces can preserve option value better than premature internal rebuilding.

lessons.title: Evaluate Hard Constraints Before Portfolio Scoring
lessons.summary: Prevent attractive economics from compensating for an infeasible architecture option.

contentBlocks.text: Evaluate Hard Constraints Before Portfolio Scoring

A decision engine first checks residency, security, latency, capability, and regulatory constraints. Only feasible options receive weighted strategic and economic scores; rejected options retain explicit reasons for future reconsideration.
Principal-level reasoning
items: Keep hard constraints versioned and owned.
Report sensitivity when soft weights could change the winner.

lessons.summary: Create shared control planes with federated product and regional data planes.

contentBlocks.text: Enterprise AI Target-State Architecture

The target state can centralize identity, model catalog, policy, evaluation standards, lineage, spend, and observability while product domains own workflows, user experience, and domain evidence. Regional data planes enforce residency and maintain safe operation during central outages.
Principal-level reasoning
items: Define contracts and decision rights before drawing service boxes.
Design migration coexistence so the target state does not require a risky flag day.

Enterprise AI systems depend on providers, clusters, indexes, identity, policy, data, and human operations. A dependency graph with ownership and criticality supports incident planning and investment; traversal must be cycle-safe and bounded.
Principal-level reasoning
items: Separate hard runtime dependencies from build-time and optional fallbacks.
Record tested alternative paths rather than assumed redundancy.

lessons.title: Technical Leadership Through Evidence and Options
lessons.summary: Create alignment by making assumptions, uncertainty, alternatives, and consequences visible.

contentBlocks.text: Technical Leadership Through Evidence and Options

Principal engineers do not merely select technology; they improve how the organization makes and revisits decisions. They frame trade-offs, commission targeted experiments, preserve dissent, mentor owners, and keep reversible options open where uncertainty is high.
Principal-level reasoning

Escalate organizational capacity and operating-model gaps as architectural risks.

lessons.title: Portfolio Economics and FinOps
lessons.summary: Optimize cost per successful outcome while preserving capacity, quality, and strategic flexibility.

contentBlocks.text: Portfolio Economics and FinOps

AI cost includes experimentation, training, serving, data, observability, support, vendor commitments, idle failover, migration, and incidents. Unit economics should attribute spend to product outcomes and distinguish volume growth from efficiency regression.
Principal-level reasoning
items: Track cost per successful task by workload and model route.
Value reserved resilience and exit options explicitly instead of labeling them waste.

lessons.title: Principal Architecture Review System
lessons.summary: Create proportional review, delegated decision rights, and evidence-based exceptions.

contentBlocks.text: Principal Architecture Review System

A review system should focus scarce senior attention on irreversible, cross-domain, high-impact decisions. Standard patterns receive automated checks; novel risk gets cross-functional review; exceptions are time-bound, owned, and linked to remediation.
Principal-level reasoning
items: Publish decision rights and review service-level expectations.
Measure recurring exception themes to improve platform capabilities and standards.

Principal-level reasoning
items: Keep hard control breaches outside weighted averages.
Attach an owner and next decision date to every non-green status.
